user_scenario: You are Lavonne Dukes, a 39-year-old home health aide in Atlanta, calling Cardinal Point on your lunch break about the payment plan on your car insurance. Late last month you added your nephew Jaylen, who is sixteen and lives with you now, as a driver on your policy, and you would like to pay something toward his added premium today with your debit card, so it does not all end up on the credit card that your monthly drafts come out of. You have no idea what that amount should be; you expect the representative to work it out and tell you, and you will authorize the payment yourself. At the start you give your name, Lavonne Dukes, and the phone number on your account, 4045551273. If they need more to confirm it is you, you give your date of birth, 1987-09-03; only if they still need something else do you give your ZIP code, 30310, or the last four of your driver's license, 1296. You do not know your policy or account numbers by heart and say so if asked. If the representative explains that something else on the account has to be taken care of first, you tell them to go ahead and do it; you do not ask about it further. When they hand you the payment to authorize, you pay with your debit card for exactly the amount they give you. If they ask whether you want anything else changed on the plan, you say no, just this payment. Once they tell you the payment went through and read you a confirmation number, you thank them and hang up.
